title: Billing export validation job + fixes for incorrect prorated invoice lines
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Customers have reported invoice amounts that differ from dashboard usage and subscription expectations. Root cause analysis across the billing pipeline (metering -> rate-limiter -> usage-aggregation -> billing-exports) identified two classes of failures: 1) an edge case in the proration calculator for mid-cycle plan changes that double-counted partial-cycle usage when a usage-based addon was present, and 2) intermittent truncation of usage export rows when Redis-backed batching timed out, which caused Stripe export jobs to create line items with missing usage units. Scope: - Fix proration math for plan-change transitions (monthly subscriptions + usage addons) - Harden the export job to deduplicate and validate rows before sending to Stripe/NetSuite - Add an async reconciliation/validation job that compares daily export summary to aggregated usage totals and emits anomalies to PagerDuty - Backfill affected invoices for the last 90 days. Proposed fix: - Implement corrected proration routine with explicit state machine (before_change, change_point, after_change) and add unit + property-based tests - Modify export worker to: 1) add per-export checksum, 2) validate required fields (units, price_id, period_start/end), 3) write rejected rows to a quarantine topic for manual review - Create validator job that runs daily to compare aggregated usage (canonical store) vs exported totals and generates a reconciliation report. Rollout: staged deploy to staging -> canary on 5% of production -> full rollout. For invoice backfill: generate corrected line items and create credit invoices when safe; for customers with large bills run manual review. Monitoring: add new dashboards for export row counts, quarantine rate, proration error rate, and a reconciliation anomaly metric. Communication: coordinate with Billing Ops and Finance to hold a freeze on automatic invoice finalization during backfill window. Links: Confluence runbook and design doc provided below.
